date_and_recency: Yegge post 1 Jan 2026. DoltHub post 15 Jan 2026. Bonacci X post: status ID suggests about late Jan / early Feb 2026 [uncertain, exact date not seen]. HBR piece March 2026 (replyfabric PDF metadata dated 8 Apr 2026 is a copy date, not publication).
key_claims: Yegge: Gas Town orchestrates many Claude Code instances, is complex, expensive, unsafe for most users, and needs an experienced multi-agent user. Sehn: watching about 20 parallel agents was too much to comprehend, so he watched only the coordinating 'Mayor' thread, felt stress, and shut it down. Bonacci (secondary only): capability to start many parallel tasks removes the natural friction that forced prioritisation, leaving him exhausted by managing rather than doing.
headline_figures: Sehn: about $100 in Claude tokens for a 60-minute session, which he says is about 10x a normal Claude Code session per unit time; roughly 20 other agents running. These are one person's single session. Yegge: 'Stage 7: 10+ agents, hand-managed.' No statistics.
sample_unit_and_population: Individual anecdotes. Yegge is a veteran software engineer; Sehn is a software engineer and DoltHub founder/CEO; Bonacci is a software engineer and startup founder. n=1 each. Not a sample.
observed_vs_stated: Stated, self-reported experience. Sehn's is a first-hand narrative of one observed session but his feelings are self-report. Nothing measured.
what_makes_oversight_tiring: Sehn: too many parallel agent threads to follow, so he drops to watching one; speed of change. Bonacci (secondary): managing many concurrent worktrees and half-finished features, loss of the friction that limited how much one started. Yegge: system complexity and the need to hand-manage many agents.
consequence_for_quality: Sehn: a pull request merged autonomously despite failing integration tests; he stopped the session. Yegge says he has never seen the code. Bonacci (secondary): feeling of losing the plot, finishing little. All anecdotal, no measured error rates.
what_reduces_the_load: Sehn: narrowing attention to a single coordinating thread (Mayor) and 'letting go', i.e. giving up detailed oversight, which is arguably the opposite of reducing load safely. Yegge: only use it if already at an advanced stage of agent use; hands-on-the-wheel management. Bonacci: not established from an opened source.
limitations_stated: Yegge says the project is chaotic, sloppy, unsafe, expensive and early. Sehn describes a single session on a tool he was trying out. Bonacci's post not read.
counter_evidence: Another early reviewer (dev.to, 10 hours with Gas Town; seen in search results only, not opened) framed the work as a manager role where span of control tracks attention and memory. Sceptical blog takes call the tool aggressive and expensive. Gas Town is an extreme, deliberately experimental setup, so these accounts may not generalise to ordinary single-agent use. Anecdotes from tool vendors and enthusiasts carry selection and incentive bias.
verification_status: Sehn/DoltHub quotes: checked against the original page (opened). Yegge warnings: checked against a full-text mirror, not Medium directly; mostly verified, re-check before quoting. Yegge launch date 1 Jan 2026: mirror and search snippets agree. Bonacci quote and post title: NOT checked against the X post (HTTP 402) [uncertain]; title and quote appear only in secondary sources. The HBR 'too much going on' attribution: the HBR/36Kr text attributes it to an unnamed 'early user'; the matching original is Sehn at DoltHub, found by search and opened. That the HBR sentence refers to Sehn is an inference [uncertain]. Original HBR article not opened.
usable_claim: Developers who tried orchestrating many agents described it as hard to follow. Tim Sehn of DoltHub wrote after a Gas Town session, 'there's really too much going on for you to reasonably comprehend', and he ended up watching one thread and closing the tool. This is one person's account, not evidence of how common it is. Yegge himself warned in his launch post that Gas Town is complicated and not safe for most users.
do_not_use: Do not quote Bonacci verbatim or attribute the 'Six worktrees' passage to him from an opened source until the X post is read. Do not say Yegge reported being fatigued. Do not present the $100/10x cost as a general figure. Do not treat any of these as data on prevalence of agent fatigue. Do not state that HBR's 'early user' is definitely Sehn.
